description: Teams chats, channels and teams as objects: the conversation's own record the Teams capture saves in the conversation's unit (integrations/capture_teams.py CONVERSATION; ontology/project_graph.py TeamsCaptures relations chats, channels, teams), each gated per conversation unit by its latest captured membership and the people exclusion, as its messages are. Messages link to their conversation (TeamsChatMessage.in_chat, TeamsChannelMessage.in_channel, generated with their types: ontology/generator/graph_families.json), a channel to its team. Participants are Entra object ids with directory display names and work addresses; a Person is formed per reader from them by the people graph.

object_types.description: One captured Teams chat (Graph chat): its topic, type, creation, latest captured message time and participants. Cited teams-chat://<chat>/conversation@<generation>-<capture-id> in the chat's own unit (teams:chat:<chat>): the reader needs that unit granted and the chat's latest captured membership (decided per handle by CaseRuntime.resolve_citation, as for its messages), so a reader who cannot read the chat sees neither the chat nor its participants. A member whose visible history starts after the chat's latest message does not see it. Source text is untrusted.

properties.name: topic
properties.description: The chat's topic (a group or meeting chat; a one-on-one chat has none).

properties.name: last_activity_at
properties.description: The latest creation or edit time of a message of this conversation the capture holds (the conversation's last captured activity), when the record was saved.

properties.name: last_updated
properties.description: Graph lastUpdatedDateTime: when the chat was renamed or its members last changed.

properties.name: participants
properties.description: The conversation's members as read with its latest captured membership: each participant's Entra object id (the shared key the people graph resolves a Person by, operating/people_graph.py), display name and work address (directory facts every employee sees: unmarked). Phone numbers, personal addresses, department and job title are never captured here. An excluded person never appears: the capture refuses a conversation with an excluded member, and the case runtime withholds the whole record from every reader when a participant is excluded later.

properties.name: participants_basis
properties.description: How the participants were read: chat_members, channel_members, team_members (a standard channel is its team's audience) or group_fallback (the team's group admits readers and names nobody: participants is empty).

object_types.description: One captured Teams channel (Graph channel): its name, description, membership type, creation, latest captured message time, participants and team. Cited teams-channel://<team>/<channel>/conversation@<generation>-<capture-id> in the channel's own unit (teams:channel:<team>/<channel>), gated as its messages are (the unit grant and the channel's latest captured membership), so a reader who cannot read the channel sees neither the channel nor its participants. Source text is untrusted.

properties.name: last_activity_at
properties.description: The latest creation or edit time of a message of this conversation the capture holds (the conversation's last captured activity), when the record was saved.

properties.name: participants
properties.description: The conversation's members as read with its latest captured membership: each participant's Entra object id (the shared key the people graph resolves a Person by, operating/people_graph.py), display name and work address (directory facts every employee sees: unmarked). Phone numbers, personal addresses, department and job title are never captured here. An excluded person never appears: the capture refuses a conversation with an excluded member, and the case runtime withholds the whole record from every reader when a participant is excluded later.

properties.name: participants_basis
properties.description: How the participants were read: chat_members, channel_members, team_members (a standard channel is its team's audience) or group_fallback (the team's group admits readers and names nobody: participants is empty).

object_types.description: One Microsoft Teams team (Graph team): its name, description and creation, read with the record of its first standard channel (by unit) that has a captured membership and cited by that record (teams-channel://<team>/<channel>/conversation@...): a standard channel's audience is the team's members, so that channel's unit and membership gate the team. A team none of whose standard channels is captured is not projected.

link_types.name: in_team
link_types.description: The team a channel belongs to (Graph structure: the channel's team id).

wb.capture_teams.note: TeamsCapture: the conversation record (conversation_row) saved with every finished or capped read of a chat or channel, after its members cleared the people guard; gated by the unit's latest membership (unit_acl).
